title.narrative: Carter Center: Promoting Participatory Rights of Women and Youth in Zambia
Carter Center: Promoting Participatory Rights of Women and Youth in Zambia

description.narrative:
Carter Center har ansökt om stöd från ambassaden om SEK 15 993 850 för att genomföra projektet '' Främja deltagande rättigheter för kvinnor och ungdomar '' i Zambia (2019-2021). Projektets mål är att verka för policyförändringar i Zambia som skyddar och främjar rätten att delta i den offentliga debatten för kvinnor och ungdomar. Projektets specifika mål är:
1. Partnerorganisationer i civila samhället har kapacitet att genomföra reformer och påverkanskampanjer för att stärka rätten att deltaga (med tonvikt på kvinnor och ungdomar), informerade av mänskliga rättigheter och rekommendationer från valobservationer. 2. Partnerorganisationer i civila samhället, regering och andra viktiga intressenter har ett aktivt och konstruktivt engagemang för stärkta deltaganderättigheter och politik och lagstiftning som integrerar ett jämställdhets- och ungdomsperspektiv. 3. Partnerorganisationer i civila samhället bidrar till en ökning av positiva berättelser om deltagande i offentligheten av kvinnor och ungdomar i medier (traditionella och nya).
Genom direkt genomförande och genom vidareförmedling till nationella partnerorganisationer kommer Carter Center att stärka det civila samhällets förmåga att verka för skapandet och efterlevnaden av lagstiftning och standarder som skyddar och främjar deltagarrättigheter. Centret kommer också att underlätta konstruktiva samråd och samarbete inom det civila samhället och mellan civilsamhället och relevanta statliga organ samt demokratiska institutioner gällande övervakning av genomförandet av mänskliga rättigheter, relevanta lagar och organisatoriska åtaganden relaterade till kvinnors och ungdomars deltagande i val. Slutligen kommer Carter Center och dess samarbetsparter att arbeta för att öka förekomsten av positiva medieberättelser om politiskt aktiva ungdomar och kvinnor.
Av den totala budgeten på SEK 15 993 850 kommer Carter Center att vidareförmedla 19% (SEK 3 008 445) av medlen till lokala organisationer i det civila samhället. Dessa kommer att väljas ut efter en kartläggningsfas. Ambassaden kommer att finansiera hela budgeten.

The Carter Center has applied for support from the Embassy amounting to SEK15 993 850 to implement the ''Promoting Participatory Rights of Women and Youth in Zambia (2019-2021) Project. The goal of the Project is to advocate for policy changes in Zambia that protect and promote the right to participate in public affairs of Women and youths. The specific objectives of the Project are: 1. CSO partners have the capacity to conduct reform and advocacy campaigns to advance participatory rights (with emphasis on women and youth), informed by human rights and election observation recommendations. 2. CSO partners, Government and other key stakeholders constructively engage to improve implementation of participatory rights and gender and youth sensitive/responsive policies and legislation. 3. CSOs contribute to an increase in positive media (traditional and new) narratives on public participation of women and youth.
Through direct implementation and sub-grants to national partner organizations, the Center will strengthen the capacity of civil society to advocate for the creation of and adherence to legislation and standards that protect and promote participatory rights. The Center will also seek to facilitate constructive consultation and collaboration within civil society and between civil society. It will also facilitate dialogue between civil society and relevant government bodies and democratic institutions on monitoring implementation of human rights obligations, relevant laws and organizational commitments related to the participation of women and youth in elections. Finally, the Center and its partners will work to increase positive media narratives on politically active youth and women.
Out of the total SEK15 993 850 the Center will forward 19% (SEK3 008 445) of the funds to local CSOs to be selected once their mapping is complete. The Embassy will fund the entire budget.

Project Goal: By late 2021, Carter Center CSO partners advocate for substantive policy changes in Zambia that protect and promote the right to participate in public affairs of women and youth. Objectives:1. CSO partners have the capacity to conduct reform and advocacy campaigns to advance participatory rights (with emphasis on women and youth), informed by human rights and election observation recommendations. 2. CSO partners, Government and other key stakeholders constructively engage to improve implementation of participatory rights and gender and youth sensitive/responsive policies and legislation. 3. CSOs contribute to an increase in positive media (traditional and new) narratives on public participation of women and youth.

The program evaluation, carried out in 2022 and conducted by an external consultant, found that the program contributed to the intended objectives set out. The contribution used two different advocacy approaches, where some partners were working on the grassroots level in rural areas and others advocating with national officials. These two approaches appeared to have complemented each other. The evaluator noted that the objectives are somewhat challenging to measure. However, it is also recognised that it may be a challenge for democracy, rights and governance programming to create objectives that focuses on measuring specific changes in a system that the programme itself cannot always control.
In general, partners stated that they felt that there was somewhat of a change in civic space as a result of the program, though the implementation period was viewed as too short by many interviewees. Nevertheless, several people felt that there may have been some changes in civic space related to women and youth participation in governance issues. The majority of partners stated that the financial resources were the most immediately impactful form of support from the Carter Center (TCC), followed by the impact of capacity strengthening training and mentoring provided by TCC and TCC-hired consultants. To mention a few key numbers related to the results, TCC provided sub-grants equaling to at least $68,500 each to 7 partner organizations and provided at least $5,000 microgrants each to 12 community-based organizations during the two year implementation period. When it comes to trainings, TCC provided capacity-building (CB) training to 154 individuals from 64 organizations. The CB workshops had a wide range of topics, including democratic election standards, financial management and oversight, evidence based advocacy and other organising strategies. TCC implemented a Community-based organisation (CBO) training session in four provinces to enhance CBO's capacity to implement governance programs seeking to strengthen women and youth participation outside of Lusaka. They also trained over 700 CSO/CBO leaders on the participation of women and youth issues as well as approximately 500 election observers. Overall, the sub-grants that TCC provided to different organisations have been successful in achieving the project goals and objectives. The organisations ZNWL and AAAZ are good examples of this. Zambia National Women Lobby (ZNWL) received a sub-grant for their project Grooming women leaders for effective participation in decision-making and governance processes at community and national levels. Their activities focused on leadership development for aspiring women leaders and those interested in running for elected office or serve as leaders in local communities. A ZNWL partner stated that the support has contributed to capacity building of the organisation and promoted womens participation in leadership and development as well as on the local level. For example the training of 89 female aspiring leaders resulted in 41 being adopted by different political parties to contest the 2021 general elections at the local government level. One female councilor, Mubutu Mwangwlwa from the Kashamu ward in Kaomo district in Western province, stated that she benefited especially from the capacity building workshops. She stated that her public speaking skills were improved through this training and that this allowed her to better share her work plan with community members, thus creating accountability and confidence to mobilise and engage with the community and traditional leaders. In December 2021, she was also elected as the Chairperson for the Planning Committee in the Kaomo Council, which according to her was due to her assertiveness and eloquence. Alliance for Accountability Advocates Zambia (AAAZ) received a grant for their project Enhancing Youth and Young Women's Participation in Governance (EYYWGP)". This programme aimed at increasing the number of youth and young women in governance. In the end of the programme, the number of youth CSO leaders in the four target provinces had increased. The programme successfully trained 101 youth CSO leaders, 76 youth engaged directly with decision makers and over 3000 youth was reached through an online survey that introduced concepts on the right to participation. A success story worth mentioning is the one on AAAZ member Emmanuel Zulu. Emmanuel participated in awareness raising and training sessions and then started raising awareness through a democracy walk where he emphasised the importance of youth and young women's inclusion in decision making spaces. This walk attracted many other young people to take part and inspired them to be more involved in decision making processes as well as to have the confidence to hold duty bearers accountable. The walk finished at the Ministry of Justice where Emmanuel and other youth called on the Ministry to support legal reforms to ensure youth inclusion in governance processes. The action received great media coverage, which also has been good for raising the awareness around these topics. Furthermore, the funding provided by Sida through TCC was vital to the implementation of partner programming. The support for capacity strengthening has contributed to long-term sustainability in how partners approach programming and work to strengthen their organisations from a financial management, mission and administrative perspective. Adding to this, the upcoming UPR (Universal Periodic Review) Shadow Report will be an evidence-based form of advocacy that is directly connected to the programme. In addition to achieving the program objectives, several unintended outcomes were produced, e.g. increased partner collaboration and partner membership, geographical expansion of activities, the use of program learning to other existing work streams and new funding. Increased collaboration among CSOs has resulted in a group of local CSOs producing a shadow report on the upcoming Universal Peer Review on the performance of the Zambian Government in promoting and safeguarding human rights
